stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Scrub time $t$ with the slider. Watch $\vec{OM}$, $\vec{v}$ (tangent to the path) and $\vec{a}$ redraw at each instant. Note how $|\vec{v}|$ and $|\vec{a}|$ change along the trajectory.
stages.concept: Vectorial kinematics: $\vec{v} = \dfrac{d\vec{OM}}{dt}$ (always tangent to the path), $\vec{a} = \dfrac{d\vec{v}}{dt}$. The angle $(\vec{v}, \vec{a})$ tells whether motion is accelerating ($<90°$), decelerating ($>90°$) or purely curving ($=90°$).

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Move the slider to the requested time. Read $|\vec{v}|$ from the HUD, then press CONFIRM. Nail all three target times to advance.
stages.concept: The three probes exercise different signatures: $|\vec{v}|$ constant on a circle (uniform circular motion), $|\vec{v}|$ linear in $t$ on a straight line with constant $\vec{a}$, $|\vec{v}|$ minimum at the vertex of a parabola.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The $\vec{v}$ arrows are hidden. At each marked point, drag the small handle to sketch the direction of $\vec{v}$. When all three are set, press SUBMIT. You have a limited number of attempts — reason before you drag.
stages.concept: $\vec{v}$ is always tangent to the trajectory in the direction of motion. Use the trajectory shape and the sense of travel (increasing $t$) to fix each arrow — no magnitude required, only direction.

labels.tip1: scrub t, watch OM, v, a redraw
labels.tip3: drag each arrow tangent to the path, in the direction of motion
labels.peek_tip_tangent: v is ALWAYS tangent to the trajectory. Look at the local slope of the curve at the marked point.
labels.peek_tip_direction: v points in the direction of motion (increasing t). If M moves rightward on the curve, v points rightward.
labels.peek_tip_circle: On a circle, v is perpendicular to OM only if O sits at the centre. Trust the tangent to the shape, not the vector to O.

1.1: Drag the time slider back and forth. What stays fixed and what changes?
1.2: v is always tangent to the path; a points toward the concave side of the curve.
1.3: When |v| grows with time, the motion accelerates: the angle (v, a) is acute. When |v| shrinks, the angle is obtuse.

2.1: The HUD shows the current t and |v|. Match the requested t within tolerance, then CONFIRM.
2.2: You do not need to compute anything — position M at the requested instant and read the magnitude from the HUD.
2.3: If a target seems out of reach, check the slider covers 0 to T. Every target sits inside that range by construction.

3.1: For each marked point, the direction of v is fixed by the shape of the trajectory at that point.
3.2: Tangent to the curve, in the sense of increasing t. If M moves left-to-right on that segment, the arrow points to the right.
3.3: For a circle traced counter-clockwise, v at the top points left; at the bottom it points right. Same shape, opposite sense = opposite arrow.
